newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Computershare wins Malaysian MESDAQ deal.
newsitem.headline: Computershare wins Malaysian MESDAQ deal.

text.p: Software developer Computershare Ltd (CSL) said on Monday it won the contract to provide a new automated equities trading, information and surveillance system for the just-established Malaysian automated share exchange.

The new exchange, run by the Malaysian Exchange of Securities Dealing & Automated Quotations Bhd (MESDAQ) and modelled on markets like NASDAQ and JASDAQ, was expected to start trading in the fourth quarter of 1997, Computershare said.

"The new MESDAQ trading system is based on CSL's successful ASTS software (Automated Securities Trading System) which is already installed in the Shanghai, Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges and the Moscow and Kazakhstan interbank currency exchanges," Computershare said.
CSL has also won contracts to set up automated stock exchanges in Helsinki, Istanbul and Cyprus.
Computershare did not say how much the contract was worth.
Computershare shares were 10 cents firmer at A$8.10 at 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT).
